note: સાર — teaching units derived from the books. Every quoted verse has been checked word-for-word against the printed page image (spellings follow the print, including its older orthography like છૂટચાં and its typesetting quirks like દુલર્ભ). Interpretations follow the tradition's own commentary (Samagam) wherever it exists. See tools/TEACHINGS_GUIDE.md for how to add units.

body_en: In the fifteenth century, in Kashi, a weaver named Kabir sang something dangerous and simple: God is one, beyond every form, and no ritual, caste, or scripture-recitation can reach Him — only love can. Tradition holds Kabir as the disciple of the Vaishnav teacher Ramanand, and from that meeting of streams — Ram's devotion and Kabir's fearless plainness — our path takes its name: Ramkabir.

Kabir's teaching travelled to Gujarat. In the 1470s, at Patan, two figures organized it into a living community: Shri Padmanabhji and Dhanraj Pandya, whom we remember as Adhyaruji Maharaj. The kirtans Adhyaruji composed — the Ganpati no Ras, the Vani, the Dhols — are the very ones this app carries, still sung five and a half centuries later.

Two centuries after that, the flame was carried by Sadguru Shri Jivanji Maharaj (1649–1737). After long years of seeking he met his guru, Gopaldas, in 1683, and on Sharad Purnima of 1688 the Uda parampara emerged. The Patidar families who followed this path stopped observing caste rules at the thali — they ate together, with everyone. Other Patels called them 'juda' — different. Juda became Uda, and what began as a taunt was worn as a badge: Uda Bhakt. Different, on purpose, for bhakti's sake.

Jivanji Maharaj settled at Puniyad, near Dabhoi, which remains a dham of the parampara. His sakhis and Adhyaruji's kirtans together form our Parayan. The Samagam of Shree Haridas Nadiyada explains the path's philosophy; Sant Darshan tells the lives of its saints. From the villages of South Gujarat the community travelled — to Africa and Fiji, to England and America — carrying pothis, building mandirs, and singing the same Vani in every new country.

The sakhi below — from the Jivandasji ki Sakhi in this app — is the tradition telling its own origin. Read the village names slowly: this is not mythology from far away. This is your family's own address.
story.anchor_verse:
कानम पे करुणा करी । प्रगटे गाहेज गाम ॥
शाहपरे समागम करी । आये है पुनियाद धाम ॥१॥
कणबी कुळ ओधारवा । जीवण लीया अवतार ॥
कृष्णदास पे कृपा सुणी । धना हुवा तैयार ॥२॥
भरम भोजाको तोडवा । केशव करवा सहाय ॥
रामबाईके दुःख फेडवा । द्वापरसे कलजुग आय ॥३॥
संत गोपालको शरण दीया । पहोचे मनके कोड ॥
एसे सद्गुरु जीवण भये । भवके बंधन छोड ॥४॥
नाना गोपाल के संग चले । आये पुनियाद धाम ॥
उदित धरम उदा कहै । रामकबीरका नाम ॥५॥
story.anchor_meaning_en: Showing karuna on the Kanam region, he appeared at Gahej village; holding samagam at Shahpara, he came to Puniyad dham. To uplift the Kanbi families, Jivan took avatar; hearing of his kripa on Krishnadas, Dhana became ready. To break Bhoja's delusion, to aid Keshav, to end Rambai's sorrows, he came as Dwapar turned to Kaliyug. He gave saint Gopal refuge and the heart's longings were fulfilled — such a Sadguru Jivan came to be, releasing the bonds of worldly existence. Walking with Nana Gopal he came to Puniyad dham; the Uda dharma arose, they say, bearing Ram-Kabir's name.
story.caveat_en: Dates and lineage follow the community's own tradition (Sadguru Shree Jivanji Maharaj Memorial Foundation).
story.anchor_verse_translit:
Kanam pe karuna kari, pragate Gahej gaam ||
Shahpare samagam kari, aaye hai Puniyad dhaam ||1||
Kanbi kul odharva, Jivan liya avtar ||
Krishnadas pe kripa suni, Dhana huva taiyar ||2||
Bharam Bhojako todva, Keshav karva sahay ||
Rambaike dukh fedva, Dwaparse Kaljug aay ||3||
Sant Gopalko sharan diya, pahoche manke kod ||
Ese Sadguru Jivan bhaye, bhavke bandhan chhod ||4||
Nana Gopal ke sang chale, aaye Puniyad dhaam ||
Udit dharam Uda kahai, Ramkabirka naam ||5||

themes.intro_en: The Vani — 'Parbrahm vani re…' — is the composition our family sings most. These three pearls walk through what it actually says, verse by verse.

units.title_en: When the voice weds the Divine
units.verse_gu:
પરબ્રહ્મ વાણી રે પરણી એ । બ્રહ્માંડ જય જયકાર રે ॥
ચાર ખાણ હવી નિર્મલી । ભાગ્યો મોહ સંસાર રે ॥૧॥
units.verse_translit: Parbrahm vani re parni e, brahmand jay jaykar re; chaar khaan havi nirmali, bhagyo moh sansar re.

gloss.meaning: the four sources of birth — egg-born, womb-born, moisture-born, seed-sprouted; i.e. all living beings

units.meaning_en: The kirtan opens with a marriage: the voice is wedded to Parabrahma. Not 'the voice praises' or 'the voice describes' — wedded. And the moment that union happens, the whole universe answers with jaykar, all four kinds of living beings become pure, and the grip of attachment breaks.
units.why_en: This is why our tradition's central act is singing, not silent study. In Adhyaruji's image, bhajan is not a report about God — it IS the union. The mouth that sings the Vani is, in that moment, married to what it sings.
units.reflect_en: My voice weds whatever it repeats every day. What does it repeat most — and what would change if the first words of my morning were these?

units.verse_gu:
લેખાં તે વાલ્યાં જમ તણાં । ઊઠીયા નરક વેહેપાર રે ॥
બંધન છૂટચાં રે જીવનાં । સહું મુગતું હોએ આવાર રે ॥૨॥
મુકતા સૌ સ્થાવર જંગમ । મુકતા સુર નર નાગ રે ॥
મુકતા સપ્ત ઋષિ નવગ્રહે । મુકતા મુનિવર જાગ રે ॥૩॥
units.verse_translit: Lekha te valyan jam tana, uthiya narak vehepar re; bandhan chhutya re jivana, sahu mugtu hoe aavar re. Mukta sau sthavar jangam, mukta sur nar nag re…

gloss.meaning: the unmoving (trees, mountains) and the moving (creatures)

units.meaning_en: When the Vani sounds, Yama closes his ledgers — hell's business shuts down for lack of customers. And notice who gets freed: not the singer alone. Trees and animals, gods, humans, serpents, the seven rishis, the nine planets — everything, still and moving, is liberated together.
units.why_en: In this path, mukti is never a private prize. That is why kirtan is sung in sabha, together, and why the Uda tradition insisted on one thali for everyone: a liberation that excludes anyone isn't the one Adhyaruji sang about.
units.reflect_en: Do I treat my spiritual life as a personal account to settle — or as something my whole ghar (household), and everything around it, shares in?

units.verse_gu:
હરિ હર બ્રહ્મા આનંદિયા । ઘેર ઘેર ઓચ્છવ હોય રે ॥
ઉલટ હોય રે અતિ ઘણો । ગાઈસું વાણીનો નાહો રે ॥૪॥
units.verse_translit: Hari Har Brahma aanandiya, gher gher ochchhav hoy re; ulat hoy re ati ghano, gaisu vanino naho re.
units.meaning_en: Vishnu, Shiva and Brahma themselves rejoice; every single home becomes a festival. The proof that the Word has arrived is not solemnity — it is ulat — joy too big to hold in, and the resolve: 'I will sing the Lord of this Vani.'
units.why_en: This verse is the seed of our Occhav tradition — the festival kirtans, as on Sharad Purnima, the very night the Uda parampara began. In this path, celebration is not a break from devotion; it is devotion's evidence.
units.reflect_en: When bhakti visits our home, does it look like a duty being performed — or like an ochhav breaking out?

themes.intro_en: The most radical thing our tradition ever did was at the dinner thali. This path explains why — in the tradition's own words.

units.title_en: One essence, after all the books
units.verse_gu:
હરિ હરિ વેદ પુરાણ સ્મૃતિ ષટદર્શન ॥
નિઘંટ વિચારી સ્વામી જોઈયું એ ॥૧॥
હરિ હરિ એક જ સાર સનાતન લાધું એ ॥
ચૈતન હરિ પરબ્રહ્મ તણું એ ॥૨॥
units.verse_translit: Hari Hari Ved Puran Smruti Shatdarshan || Nighant vichari Swami joiyu e ||1|| Hari Hari ek j saar sanatan ladhu e || Chaitan Hari Parbrahm tanu e ||2||

gloss.meaning: the six classical schools of Hindu philosophy
lexicons, glossaries — the reference books of scholarship

units.meaning_en: Adhyaruji opens the Ved Puran with a claim of method, not rejection: I went through it all — Vedas, Puranas, Smritis, all six schools of philosophy, even the lexicons — and examined them. What survived the search was a single eternal essence: the living, conscious Hari Parabrahma.
units.why_en: This is why the tradition's stance on scripture is transcendence, not contempt. The kirtan does not say the books are worthless; it says they were read, weighed, and found to point past themselves. Everything else this path teaches — the one thali, bhakti over ritual — stands on this verse's authority: the conclusion of a man who did the reading.
units.reflect_en: Have I examined what I inherited — or only either obeyed it or dismissed it?

units.verse_gu:
આશ્રમે દર્શને વર્ણે જે ભોલવ્યા ।
તું વિના સહુ એ રડવડાએ ॥૪૧॥
units.verse_translit: Aashrame darshane varne je bholavya, tu vina sahu e radvadae.
units.meaning_en: Whoever put their trust in life-stage, in philosophical schooling, in caste — all of them, says Adhyaruji, wander lost without You. Identity is not a boat. Learning is not a boat. Birth is certainly not a boat. Only devotion crosses.
units.why_en: This is not our interpretation — it is the Samagam's own. On its opening pages the Samagam quotes exactly this charan to explain why Uda bhaktas do not observe varnashram at meals: 'Adhyarujina Ved Puranna 41ma charanne batavine kahe chhe ke Uda bhakto varnashramma manta nathi.' One verse, and a community stopped ranking people at the thali. That verse is the charter of the Uda name.
units.reflect_en: Which credential of mine — degree, surname, seniority — do I quietly treat as a boat?

themes.intro_en: Sant Darshan opens its very cover with two sakhis about what a saint is and why company matters more than effort. They set the lens for every life story in that book.

units.verse_gu:
સરવર તરુવર સંતજન । ચૌથા બરસૈ મેહ ॥
પરમારથ કે કારનૈ । ચારો ધારી દેહ ॥૩॥
units.verse_translit: Sarvar taruvar santjan, chautha barsai meh; parmarath ke kaarnai, chaaro dhari deh.
units.meaning_en: A lake, a tree, a saint, and the rain: four things that take a body at all only for the sake of others. The lake doesn't drink its own water; the tree doesn't eat its own fruit; the cloud doesn't keep its rain. That is the definition of a sant.
units.why_en: Sant Darshan prints this on its cover — it is the measuring rod for every saint's life told inside. The tradition's test of holiness is not miracles or austerity; it is whether a life quenches other people's thirst.
units.reflect_en: What did my deh do for someone who can't repay me — today?

units.verse_gu:
રામ ભક્તિ સબ કો કરે । બ્રહ્મા શંકર શેષ ॥
સંત સંગત બિન જીવણા । દુલર્ભ હરિકા દેશ ॥૨॥
units.verse_translit: Ram bhakti sab ko kare, Brahma Shankar Shesh; sant sangat bin Jivna, durlabh Harika desh.

gloss.meaning: દુર્લભ — out of reach, hard to attain (the cover's typesetting transposes the conjunct)
Hari's country — the state of union with God

units.meaning_en: Everyone does Ram-bhakti — even Brahma, Shankar and Shesh do. Devotion itself is not the rare ingredient. But without the company of sants, O Jivan, Hari's country stays out of reach. The rare thing is not effort; it is company.
units.why_en: This is why the unit of practice in our tradition is the gathered sabha — the parayan circle, the bhajan mandali — and never the lone achiever. The path is walked in company or not at all.
units.reflect_en: Honestly listed: who is my sangat — the five people whose company shapes what I love?

themes.intro_en: Two pearls: what the guru IS in this tradition, and how — very concretely, with village names — grace arrived at our own doorstep.

units.title_en: The Guru is the Divine's own form
units.verse_gu:
બૂડી હું જમ ધણી વહુણી । સલૂણી એ ॥
તે સમે સમરિયા સ્વામી । સોભાગ્ય સલૂણી એ ॥૧૫॥
ગુરૂઓ એ પ્રભુ પરબ્રહ્મ સ્વરૂપ । સલૂણી એ ॥
અખિલ ભુવન તણો ઈશ । સોભાગ્ય સલૂણી એ ॥૧૬॥
units.verse_translit: Budi hun jam dhani vahuni, saluni e; te same samariya Swami, sobhagya saluni e. Guruo e Prabhu Parbrahm swarup, saluni e; akhil bhuvan tano Ish, sobhagya saluni e.

gloss.meaning: with Yama as master, without my Lord — i.e. death closing in
the dhol's refrain — 'O graceful one / O fortunate one'

units.meaning_en: The soul speaks: I was drowning, death already my master — and in exactly that moment I remembered the Swami. Then the declaration: the Guru is Parabrahma's own form, the Lord of all worlds. Not God's messenger, not God's employee — God's own shape, appearing at the drowning-point.
units.why_en: This is the tradition's answer to 'why a guru at all?' — because at the moment you are actually drowning, an idea of God cannot reach into the water. A form can. This is the reverence behind every 'Sadguru' in our books.
units.reflect_en: At my last real drowning-point, what did I actually reach for?

units.verse_gu:
कानम पे करुणा करी । प्रगटे गाहेज गाम ॥
शाहपरे समागम करी । आये है पुनियाद धाम ॥१॥
कणबी कुळ ओधारवा । जीवण लीया अवतार ॥
कृष्णदास पे कृपा सुणी । धना हुवा तैयार ॥२॥
units.verse_translit: Kanam pe karuna kari, pragate Gahej gaam; Shahpare samagam kari, aaye hai Puniyad dhaam. Kanbi kul odharva, Jivan liya avtaar; Krishnadas pe kripa suni, Dhana huva taiyar.

gloss.meaning: the Kanam region of south Gujarat
the Kanbi (Patidar) families — our own lineage

units.meaning_en: Most scriptures speak of grace in general. This sakhi gives it a map reference: karuna on Kanam, appearing at Gahej village, samagam at Shahpura, arrival at Puniyad dham — and the purpose stated outright: to uplift the Kanbi families. Jivanji's avatar, says the sakhi, was for us, by name.
units.why_en: Every family in this app descends from the kul (family line) this verse names. The Uda name, the Ramkabir naam, the books you are reading — the sakhi's own last line says where they came from: 'Udit dharam Uda kahai, Ramkabirka naam.' Gratitude, in this tradition, has an address.
units.reflect_en: If grace reached my family with village names attached — what is my generation's part of the sentence?
